Based at our welcoming Roskilde office, you will join the Workplace department, which develops and maintains BEC’s cloud-based Microsoft platform, including SharePoint and Microsoft 365 administration services, for BEC and our 25 Danish banking customers.

As a Senior Microsoft 365 Platform/System Engineer, you will join a team of dedicated professionals focused on developing SharePoint and Microsoft 365 within our Modern Workplace services.

You will be part of a cross-country, agile Microsoft 365 team comprising 12 dedicated professionals.

At BEC, we value regular in-office collaboration while offering flexibility to work remotely for up to eight days per month. You will report to Anne-Mette Bluhme.

**Your primary tasks and responsibilities will include:

**

• Developing and managing SharePoint Online Services

• Administering and maintaining the Microsoft 365 suite, including Copilot, Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, Teams and OneDrive for Business

• Ensuring the availability, performance, and security of these services

• Implementing and managing security controls for Microsoft 365 environments, ensuring compliance with industry standards and regulatory requirements

• Participation in development projects of new services

• Developing and maintaining PowerShell scripts to automate administrative tasks and improve efficiency

• Handling second-line Microsoft 365 incidents and service requests

**To succeed in this role, you should have:

**

• Solid experience in SharePoint development and maintenance

• Solid experience administering Microsoft 365 services

• Strong knowledge of Microsoft 365 applications, including Exchange Online, Teams, OneDrive for Business, and Copilot

• Knowledge of Power Apps, Power Automate, and Microsoft Purview

• Fluency in written and spoken English

• Excellent troubleshooting and problem-solving skills

• Customer-oriented thinking and high-quality standards

• The ability to collaborate effectively across functions and teams

• Curiosity, openness, and a willingness to share knowledge with others

**It would also be an advantage to have:

**

• Familiarity with cloud security and compliance standards

• Knowledge of networking and identity management in cloud environments

• Experience in the financial sector

**Be your best self with BEC's benefits!

**We offer a diverse range of benefits for our employees. Here are just a few of them.

• Professional development budget

• Healthy, varied lunch and fruit in the canteen

• Active staff associations: yoga, cycling, go-karting, games, bowling etc.

• Pension scheme

• Health and dentist insurance

• Referral bonus

**What does the recruitment process look like?

**

• Send us your CV: We want to get to know you

• Screening call: Let's chat and see if we're a match

• Meet your future manager and team: See who you'll be working closely with.

• Personality and cognitive test: Let's learn more about you.

• Meet our talent partner and your future manager once more: Get feedback on your test results.

• Time to sign the contract: We're ready to welcome you to BEC!

If you have any questions about the position, please contact Development Manager Anne-Mette Bluhme at abz@bec.dk.

BEC is in the process of being acquired by our largest customer and co-owner, Nykredit, which is Denmark's largest mortgage provider and third-largest bank. We will become part of a new and larger organization called Nykredit Financial Technologies. In the transition phase, we are recruiting for roles that we expect to be highly needed in our future organization.

Summary

As an Entry-level Consultant at Oliver Wyman in Copenhagen, you will join a diverse project team to address complex client challenges. Responsibilities include conducting research, analysing data, preparing deliverables such as presentations and workshops, and supporting client decision-making. The role offers flexibility to specialise early, opportunities for professional growth, and the chance to work across industries. Applicants must have a Bachelor’s degree (Master’s is also accepted), fluency in Danish or another Nordic language (Swedish, Norwegian, or Finnish), and English. The position values initiative, creativity, and strong analytical skills. Hybrid working and travel within the home market are part of the role. No specific industry experience or academic majors are required.

JOB DESCRIPTION

Who we are

Oliver Wyman is a global management consulting firm. We work with clients through their most defining moments, combining deep industry knowledge, specialized expertise, and the power of perspective to help them adapt, grow, and thrive.

We believe diverse perspectives make the work stronger. Our consultants bring different backgrounds, experiences, and ways of thinking to help solve complex problems and create lasting impact for clients, colleagues, and communities.

At Oliver Wyman, we are proud of the values that we aspire to live by. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment where everyone can thrive and reach their full potential.

What you will do

• As a member of your project team you’ll work alongside colleagues of all levels and clients worldwide to solve complex problems and drive meaningful change.

• You’ll help teams understand client challenges by conducting research, gathering data, running surveys and interviews, and turning information into clear insights.

• You’ll analyze problems, identify patterns, test hypotheses, and help structure recommendations that support client decision-making.

• You’ll contribute to client-ready deliverables, including presentations, analysis, workshops, and discussions that help move projects forward.

• You’ll have the opportunity to work across our industries and capabilities, with the flexibility to specialize early or explore different areas before choosing a path.

• You’ll likely have the chance to travel within your home market and internationally. No two weeks are ever the same.

• You’ll build core consulting skills from the start, including how to structure your work, communicate clearly, contribute to team problem-solving, and manage your priorities.

Why join us?

You can be your best here. At Oliver Wyman, you will find meaningful work, talented people, and a culture built on trust, support, and growth.

Create solutions that have impact

• Work on challenging projects that help clients solve complex problems, make better decisions, and create meaningful impact.

• Have the opportunity to work across different industries, capabilities, and cultures, contributing to work that has lasting impact for clients, industries, and society.

• Be part of teams that measure success not just by deliverables, but by the difference created together.

Develop as a leader

• From day one, be encouraged to take initiative, ask questions, and bring your perspective to the work.

• Learn how to structure problems, communicate clearly, and contribute to team discussions and client conversations.

• As you grow, you’ll have opportunities to build confidence, take on more responsibility, and develop the skills to unlock the potential of others.

Learn and grow without limits

• Learn on the job and through formal training, developing core skills in communication, presentation, analytics, problem-solving, and client management.

• Each project will give you new opportunities to learn from specialists, broaden your perspective, and build momentum in your career.

• You’ll have support around you as you grow, including a dedicated buddy, a career advisor, your talent manager, and communities that help you find your place.

Thrive in a vibrant and inclusive culture

• Work with genuine colleagues who stand by their beliefs, collaborate across differences, and support one another.

• Be part of an open, inclusive, and down-to-earth culture where diverse perspectives strengthen the work.

• Connect with colleagues through employee resource groups, office communities, and social activities.

Experience rewards that work for you

• We believe in flexibility, including hybrid working, and in helping colleagues build sustainable careers.

• Over time, you’ll have access to opportunities, programs, and experiences designed to help you perform, grow, and thrive — including non-profit fellowships, sabbaticals, and externships.

• Enjoy competitive local benefits designed to support your well-being, development, and life outside of work.

Who can apply?

• Applicants with a Bachelor´s (and Master’s) degree only are eligible to apply for this vacancy.

• We look for people who display initiative, intuition, and creativity with a strong problem solving and analytical mindset. We do not require specific academic majors or industry experience; we value diversity of experience and skills, extracurricular activities, and evidence of leading an interesting and impactful life outside of your studies.

• Language skills**:** Fluency in Danish or another Nordic language (Swedish, Norwegian, or Finnish), as well as English.

How to apply?

Please submit your CV, cover letter and transcripts. If you would like to find out more information about Oliver Wyman, please visit our website. If you're having technical issues submitting your application or any questions, please reach out to recruiting.nordics@oliverwyman.com

What to expect during the interviews process?

At Oliver Wyman, we want you to shine in your interview. Our process is designed like our work environment — it’s challenging, exciting, and fun.

With a mix of conversational and case interviews, our approach not only helps us to get to know you better, understanding your strengths and interests, but it also enables you to learn more about our people and our business.

If you want to learn more about consulting interviews and start your preparation, please visit our careers page: https://www.oliverwyman.com/careers/entry-level/interview-preparation.html

Oliver Wyman is a business of Marsh (NYSE: MRSH), a global leader in risk, reinsurance and capital, people and investments, and management consulting, advising clients in 130 countries. With annual revenue of over $27 billion and more than 95,000 colleagues, Marsh helps build the confidence to thrive through the power of perspective. For more information, visit oliverwyman.com, or follow us on LinkedIn and X.

Marsh is committed to creating a diverse, inclusive and flexible work environment. We aim to attract and retain the best people and embrace diversity of age, background, disability, ethnic origin, family duties, gender orientation or expression, marital status, nationality, parental status, personal or social status, political affiliation, race, religion and beliefs, sex/gender, sexual orientation or expression, skin color, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

Marsh is committed to hybrid work, which includes the flexibility of working remotely and the collaboration, connections and professional development benefits of working together in the office. All Marsh colleagues are expected to be in their local office or working onsite with clients at least three days per week. Office-based teams will identify at least one “anchor day” per week on which their full team will be together in person.

Do you thrive in the field, solving technical challenges and working on advanced marine systems across different locations?

On behalf of our client, MARPRO Group is looking for a skilled Field Service Mechanic to support the installation, commissioning, maintenance, and troubleshooting of advanced marine systems in Denmark and internationally.

You will become part of a highly specialised organisation working with advanced maritime and electronic systems in a demanding operational environment. The team combines technical expertise, innovation and a strong sense of purpose to deliver reliable solutions where quality, precision and commitment are essential.

The job

As a Field Service Mechanic, you will work with the installation, commissioning, service and maintenance of advanced marine equipment both in the workshop and at customer locations. A significant part of the role involves troubleshooting and repairing diesel engines, mechanical systems and hydraulic equipment to ensure reliable operation in demanding environments.

You will be responsible for diagnosing faults, carrying out repairs and overhauls, and supporting sea trials and commissioning activities. Working closely with engineers and technicians you will play an important role in resolving technical issues and ensuring that equipment performs according to specification.

The position combines workshop-based work with field assignments in Denmark and internationally and includes travel for up to 60 days per year.

People don't show up just to do a job. They show up because they have passion. We are looking for individuals with fire in their eyes and the right attitude.

Professional Qualifications

• You are educated as a Mechanic, Boat Mechanic, Ship Fitter, Diesel Mechanic, Truck Mechanic or have similar technical background

• Solid experience working with diesel engines such as Deutz, Cummins, MAN, MTU, Caterpillar, or similar, including fuel, cooling, and auxiliary systems

• Experience installing, maintaining, troubleshooting, and repairing mechanical, hydraulic, and rotating equipment

• Experience using PC-based diagnostic and engine management tools to identify faults and optimise equipment performance

• Troubleshooting

• Valid driving license

• Willingness to travel up to 60 days per year

• Fluency in English, eligibility to work within the EU, and ability to obtain EU security clearance

Personal characteristics

• Hands-on and passionate about mechanical troubleshooting and field service work

• Able to work independently and make sound technical decisions on-site

• Proactive, solution-oriented, and driven by solving technical challenges

• Reliable, flexible, and committed to delivering high-quality workmanship

• Comfortable working in changing environments and travelling as part of the role

• Customer-focused with strong communication and collaboration skills

• Eager to continuously expand technical knowledge and competencies

Our Client offers

• A competitive salary package aligned with experience and responsibilities.

• The opportunity to work with cutting‑edge technology and innovative systems.

• A professional environment with room to grow, develop and influence workflows.

• A supportive, collaborative team culture focused on high technical standards.

• Employment is subject to security clearance, ensuring a stable and trusted work setting

Application

The application process is handled by MARPRO Group. If you have any questions to this position, please contact MARPRO Group at +45 5370 0995.

If you are interested in the position, please upload a motivated application and an updated CV via the application button. You will receive a confirmation email from us. Please check your spam folder, if you have not received the confirmation within 10 minutes after applying, to ensure future communication.

We strongly encourage you to connect with MARPRO Group, to be considered for job openings that are not publicly listed. It is 100% free and confidential to join our talent pool and you can create your personal profile in few minutes.

Whether you’re a maritime or logistics company seeking exceptional professionals or a skilled individual searching for the next career opportunity, we connect the right talent with the right employers. Our extensive network and industry-specific expertise ensure a seamless recruitment process, making us the preferred choice for Maritime & Shipping staffing solutions.

Statera is a Danish software company building a web-native platform for authoring, tagging and filing financial reports. We help accountants and businesses go from bookkeeping data to finished, compliant annual reports, including iXBRL/XBRL filing, in one modern tool.

We're looking for a newly graduated developer who wants to build a product from the inside, write code that ships to production every week, and grow into real ownership of a SaaS platform used by paying customers.

What you'll work on

You'll join our small product team and work across the whole Statera platform:

• Frontend in SvelteKit, TypeScript and Tailwind

• Backend in Python with FastAPI and Polars

• Integrations with accounting systems such as e-conomic and Dinero

• Report generation, financial calculations and iXBRL/XBRL output

• AI-powered features that help users write and review their reports

You'll work closely with the founders, start on concrete tasks from our backlog, and quickly move on to owning whole features and areas of the product, from idea and design to deploy and follow-up with customers.

Example tasks

• Designing and building new features across frontend and backend

• Building and maintaining APIs and third-party integrations

• Implementing financial calculations and data processing in Python

• Working on iXBRL/XBRL generation and validation

• Building AI functionality and LLM-powered features into the product

• Fixing bugs and improving the product based on customer feedback

• Writing tests, improving code quality and keeping the platform reliable in production

• Taking part in code reviews, architecture discussions and product decisions

We imagine that you

• Have recently completed, or are about to complete, a degree in computer science, software engineering, IT, engineering or something similar

• Have solid experience with Python and/or TypeScript/JavaScript from studies, a student job or personal projects

• Are comfortable with Git and a pull request based workflow

• Are curious and quick to find your way around a new codebase

• Use AI coding tools (e.g. Claude Code, Cursor or Copilot) as a natural part of your work, and stay critical of what they produce

• Take responsibility for things actually working in production, not just on your machine

• Want to understand the customer's problem, not only the ticket

• Communicate clearly in English (Danish is a plus)

It's a plus if you have experience with

• Svelte/SvelteKit, React or other modern frontend frameworks

• FastAPI, Polars, Pandas or similar

• REST APIs, OAuth and integrations

• Docker, Kubernetes or cloud platforms

• LLMs, AI agents or machine learning

• Accounting, finance, XBRL or B2B SaaS

We care more about how you think and solve problems than about you knowing everything from day one.

What we offer

• A full-time position (37 hours per week)

• Real ownership of a product with paying customers, early in your career

• Close mentoring from experienced developers in software, MLOps and AI

• A modern tech stack and an AI-first development workflow

• A direct say in how the product and the codebase evolve

• An informal work environment with short decision paths

• Pension and health insurance

• Office in Aarhus with flexibility for remote days

How to apply

Send a short application and your CV.

We'd love a link to your GitHub or examples of code you've written: thesis projects, study projects, hobby projects, open source or anything else that shows how you work.

We care more about curiosity, ownership and the ability to make things work than about having the perfect background.

Job Description: What if your next data engineering challenge wasn't building one more solution - but shaping how 150 data engineers build theirs? At Tryg, we are bringing our analytical, AI and pricing landscape together around Databricks and building a stronger, shared engineering foundation across Scandinavia.

We are looking for a Principal Data Engineer to define what great Data Engineering looks like across Tryg - and turn those principles into frameworks, tooling and ways of working that engineers use.

You will get a broad technical mandate, significant autonomy and the opportunity to shape how Data Engineering develops across Tryg.

About the role | Shape Data Engineering across Tryg

As Principal Data Engineer, you will lead the development of Data Engineering Excellence across Tryg. Your focus goes beyond solving individual engineering challenges. You will establish the standards, reference solutions and reusable patterns that enable our teams to build reliable, scalable and maintainable data solutions.

Working closely with Platform Engineering, Lead Data Engineers, Data Architects and Principal colleagues across AI and Pricing, you will:

• Define and evolve engineering standards across development, testing, CI/CD, observability, documentation, dependency management and the use of GenAI.

• Develop reference implementations and reusable patterns that can be adopted across teams.

• Co-create frameworks, automation and platform capabilities with Platform Engineering.

• Help shape Tryg's core data architecture and engineering principles.

• Drive adoption and raise technical maturity through guidance, coaching and knowledge sharing.

A key part of your role is turning technical direction into real change. Success isn't a standard documented somewhere - it is better engineering practices becoming part of how 150+ data engineers work.

The role is an individual contributor but participates in the Data Enablement leadership team; to ensure long term decisions are anchored with deep engineering knowledge.

About you | A strong engineer who makes other engineers better

You have a strong technical background and have spent a significant part of your career designing and building complex, production-grade data solutions. Over time, your perspective has expanded from solving individual engineering problems to improving how engineering is done across teams.

You are comfortable with ambiguity. You can structure complex problems, bring together different perspectives, evaluate trade-offs and make technical decisions when alignment cannot be reached.

We imagine that you bring:

• Strong Data Engineering and software engineering fundamentals.

• Experience establishing engineering standards, frameworks or reusable patterns.

• The technical depth to make difficult decisions and explain the trade-offs behind them.

• Experience influencing senior engineers and technical leaders across teams.

• Experience driving adoption at scale - not simply defining standards but changing how teams actually work.

• Ability to think in systems – not just for technical challenges, but also how you solve interaction with large communities

Experience with Databricks, modern data platforms and cloud engineering is highly relevant. Experience from a regulated organization is an advantage, but not a requirement.

You don't need to be the deepest specialist in every data discipline. Your focus will be engineering excellence: how we design, develop, test, deploy, operate and continuously improve data solutions on a large scale – both in data volumes and complexity.

About us | Build the foundation while it is still being shaped

Tryg is one of Scandinavia's largest non-life insurance companies, serving more than 5 million customers across Denmark, Norway and Sweden.

You will join Data Enablement and become part of our strategic technical leadership. Strong engineering practices already exist across Tryg - your opportunity is to help turn the best of them into common approaches that can scale across teams.

There is no finished blueprint waiting for you to maintain. Many of the foundational choices are still being made, giving you the opportunity to leave a significant fingerprint on how Data Engineering is done at Tryg for years to come.

Employee benefits | Something to look forward to

At Tryg, we offer attractive conditions and employee benefits, including:

• An attractive pension scheme.

• General bonus programme.

• Health and dental insurance.

• Five weeks of holiday, five additional holiday days and four extra days off.

• Flexible ways of working with trust and responsibility.

You will also become part of a strong professional community with highly skilled colleagues across Tryg.

**Recruitment process | Show us how you think

**As part of the recruitment process, you will work with a case based on an open engineering challenge. We are less interested in one theoretically perfect answer and more interested in how you approach ambiguity, evaluate technical trade-offs and turn technical direction into something that can successfully be adopted at scale.

**We look forward to hearing from you

**Send us your application and CV no later than 28 October 2026. We encourage you not to include a photo in your CV.

We review applications continuously and will close the recruitment process once we have found the right candidate.

If you have any questions about the position, you are welcome to contact Andreas Harmuth at andreas.harmuth@tryg.dk

We encourage everyone regardless of gender identity, age, background, disability or origin to apply for the position. We are proud to have high employee satisfaction, strong professionalism and equal opportunities to develop your career in the Tryg Group. Tryg is the largest non-life insurance company in Scandinavia with activities in Denmark, Norway and Sweden. Every day we strive – each in our own way – to create peace of mind and affect the lives of most Scandinavians. Read more at www.tryg.com

Can you turn footage, graphics and ideas into engaging motion content, with a sharp eye for design? Join our creative team and help bring three Nordic retail brands to life.

At Whiteaway Group, we are continuing our growth journey across the Nordics, with Group Marketing playing a pivotal role. We create content and campaigns that bring customers to our online and physical stores while building our three strategic brands: Skousen, Whiteaway and Tretti.

You will join the creative design team in Group Marketing, working closely with fellow creatives, marketing specialists and media specialists to turn campaign objectives into effective visual communication.

The job

Your main focus will be motion design, animation and video editing. You understand how movement, pacing, sound and composition work together to tell a story, capture attention and make a message clear.

You will develop content from scratch and edit, adapt and repurpose existing material across channels and formats. A strong foundation in graphic design will help you create work that feels considered, consistent and true to each brand, both in motion and in still visuals.

More specifically, your tasks will be to:

• Create motion graphics and animations that bring campaign concepts, messages and brand identities to life.

• Edit video with a clear sense of narrative, rhythm and continuity, combining footage, graphics, music and sound.

• Develop content for social media, digital advertising, TV and internal communication, adapting the storytelling to each channel.

• Apply a strong eye for typography, layout, colour and composition across motion content and supporting static assets.

• Collaborate with creative, marketing and media colleagues to deliver content that meets campaign objectives and follows brand guidelines.

• Share ideas and feedback, and explore techniques and tools that improve both the work and the way we produce it.

Your profile

• You have around three years of relevant experience in motion design and video editing, with a portfolio that demonstrates your craft and creative thinking.

• You have a background in motion design, animation, graphic design or a related field.

• You are confident in Adobe After Effects and Premiere Pro, and comfortable working with Illustrator and Photoshop.

• You understand animation principles and use timing, easing and transitions purposefully.

• You have a strong sense of visual storytelling and know how editing, pacing and sound shape the viewer’s experience.

• You have a trained graphic eye and can translate a visual identity into motion while keeping the brand recognisable.

• You enjoy creating new work as well as finding effective ways to adapt existing content.

• You work in a structured way, meet deadlines and contribute openly to collaboration and creative feedback.

We offer an amazing workplace, including:

• A dynamic, ambitious organisation.

• An informal environment with short decision-making processes.

• A culture of trust that gives you room to plan your day and balance your life.

• Flexibility in how and when you work, healthcare, a lunch scheme, a gym and an active staff association, to mention just a few.

Start date, application and questions

We review applications and hold interviews on an ongoing basis, so please send your cover letter, CV and portfolio as soon as possible. Include examples of motion design and video editing, and briefly describe your contribution to the work.

If you have questions about the role, please contact Daniel Kjeldsen, Creative Lead & Manager, at dkj@whiteawaygroup.com.

Applications may be submitted in Danish or English and must be sent via the “Apply” button.

We look forward to hearing from you.

Start date: As soon as possible.

Whiteaway Group is an ambitious, successful and fast-growing e-commerce and retail company. We sell white goods and premium home products to customers throughout the Nordics via several online shops and the Skousen franchise.

The idea for Whiteaway Group arose in the backroom of a Danish kitchen store. The foundation was innovation, business acumen and excellent customer experience. And it still is. • Collaborate closely with R&D, Production, QC, Quality, and Regulatory Affairs

• Support inspections, product registrations, and technical investigations

**

• M.Sc. or Ph.D. in Organic Chemistry, Pharmaceutical Sciences, or a related field

• Hands-on experience withPreparative HPLC is essential; peptide purification experience is an advantage

• Strong understanding of organic chemistry, molecular interactions, and reaction mechanisms

• Knowledge of GMP/GLP, method validation, and pharmacopeial requirements is beneficial

• Able to work independently while thriving in a collaborative, cross-functional environment

**

• A meaningful role contributing to the development of life-saving antibiotics

• An international and collaborative work environment

• Opportunities for professional and personal development

• Collaboration with highly skilled scientists across multiple locations

• Competitive salary, bonus scheme, pension, and health insurance

Ready to shape compliance in a dynamic global company? Join KK Group as our New Legal Compliance Counsel and play a pivotal role in building and advancing our Legal Compliance function.

We are seeking a dynamic and experienced Legal Compliance Counsel in support of the expanding Legal Compliance function as part of the Legal Governance, Compliance & Projects department. Our new colleague should be a team player who can navigate the complexities of a high-growth environment and contribute to the continued success and sustainability of our organisation and business.

This role will play a big part of the ambitious growth trajectory and foster a culture of compliance awareness across our organisation and in our business activities in general.

As Legal Compliance Counsel you will be supporting the entire organisation, locally and globally. You will be responsible for driving and supporting the expansion of a Legal Compliance function, collaborating with key stakeholders throughout the organisation, and embedding legal compliance practices across all levels of the organisation.

Responsibilities

Compliance:

Develop, implement, and integrate a robust compliance framework tailored to the activities and risk profile of the entire organisation, locally and globally, entailing among others:

• Being on top of regulatory developments related to Legal Compliance, hereunder implementing and driving the organisation’s set-up in relation to NIS2, CRA, Data Act etc.

• Developing and delivering training programs to build and promote legal compliance awareness throughout the organisation.

• Leading the review and implementation of relevant global policies, guidelines and procedures.

• Driving a compliance culture with continuous improvements by assessing and enhancing processes and tools.

• Supporting PMI activities within specified legal compliance disciplines.

jobs.occupation: Professor of Geological Mapping and Mineral Resources
jobs.description:
The Geological Survey of Denmark and Greenland (GEUS) seeks excellent candidates with a strong research profile in one or more disciplines related to igneous and sedimentary rock geology, geologically applied geophysics and geochemistry, ore geology, remote sensing, tectonics and structural evolution to fill a new full professor position. The professorship focuses on Greenland and the surrounding Arctic.

  You are expected to contribute to GEUS’ overall strategy by strengthening and further developing our knowledge of the geological evolution of Greenland from a combined field geology, laboratory analysis and modelling approach. An important element is advancing the understanding of the various geological settings in Greenland with a broad scientific focus spanning from paleogeography, sedimentary basins, mountain belts and rift zones to tectonic features and associated mineral systems.

  Furthermore, you are expected to promote our ideas, expertise and concepts to the surrounding societies, to deliver research output at a high international level, and to successfully obtain funding for and lead larger research projects. Moreover, the position aims to strengthen and profile our research, public sector consultancy and advisory activities.

  The position is in the Department for Mapping and Mineral Resources, which is located at GEUS’ main office in Copenhagen.

  About the position
 The candidate is expected to establish and further develop a strong and coherent research group in the Department for Mapping and Mineral Resources, which will closely cooperate with the other departments in GEUS as well as with Danish universities and relevant international research institutions. Many of GEUS’ activities in this research field are focused on the geology of Greenland and the surrounding Arctic, and fieldwork in Greenland will be a key activity. Moreover, development and application of new, innovative methods for efficient data analysis are expected to continuously contribute to the advancement of the research field, and the professor is expected to play a central role in this context.

  Candidates for professorships at GEUS must have a strong research profile in the field and have a strong publication track record in international research journals with high impact in the research field. Moreover, candidates are expected to have played and have the ambition to play a key role in advancing the research field, for example by taking part in the organisation of international conferences and by editing relevant journals and/or book series.

  Research activities are to a large extent dependent on external funding. GEUS has a strong tradition for attracting research funding from e.g. Danish research councils, the European Commission, private foundations and authorities. GEUS also leads and acts as a partner in internationally funded research projects such as EU Horizon projects. Professors at GEUS should have a strong track record of research funding and play a leading role in research funding applications and project management.

  Professors at GEUS are expected to set the direction for GEUS’ research within their field of expertise and related fields to develop and advance research and make new ideas thrive in an open and welcoming research environment. Furthermore, professors at GEUS play an active role in career planning for early-career scientific staff and take responsibility for the supervision of PhD students and postdoctoral researchers. They are also expected to have a collaborative spirit and actively engage with other professors, project managers and staff to contribute to a dynamic research environment. Moreover, professors may become members of GEUS’ research committee and act as sparring partners for management decisions on strategic planning and hiring plans for scientific staff.

  GEUS is an independent research institution under the Danish Ministry of Climate, Energy and Utilities. GEUS provides research-based public sector consultancy for Danish governmental institutions and research-based advice to private companies. Professors are expected to take part in such public sector consultancy and act as sparring partners for colleagues and management in such matters.

  Who are you? 
 We seek candidates with an excellent international profile. Consideration will be given to your international network, your ability to engage and motivate staff, as well as your openness, drive and interpersonal skills.

  You have a research profile in the field, and you have visions and ideas for developing the research field. You are experienced in creating and establishing research projects with different partners, obtaining external funding, and in leading and managing large research projects.

  Experience with supervising MSc and PhD students as well as early-career researchers is a prerequisite.

  We also expect you to have experience with public sector consultancy, advisory activities (or similar), and fieldwork. Especially, experience with fieldwork in Greenland and/or another Arctic/Antarctic environment is considered advantageous.

  The Department for Mapping and Mineral Resources
 In the Department for Mapping and Mineral Resources, we conduct research on rocks, their mineralogy and chemical composition, and their genesis and evolution. We use this insight to provide the geological background for investment opportunities in exploration for mineral resources and data for responsible natural resource management. For this work, we have considerable in-house analytical facilities, including instruments for analysis of major and trace elements, isotopic composition and analytical microscopy.

  One of the department’s important tasks is the continuous geological mapping of Greenland. In addition to the above-mentioned tools, we acquire and analyse high-resolution stereographic images of mountain walls in our photo laboratory, which provides our geologists with a powerful tool for the development of 3D geological mapping on metres to tens of kilometres scales. Finally, the department hosts D-MIC (Danish Mineral Intelligence Centre), which analyses raw materials’ value chains, thereby linking geological knowledge to society’s need for mineral raw materials.
 
 A working environment with a focus on professional development and well-being

  There are many good reasons why you should choose a working life at GEUS.

  We are a diverse staff of about 300 committed employees. Trust and flexibility are keywords. The working environment is lively, informal and international. Our tasks are versatile and there are plenty of opportunities for you to influence the development of your task portfolio.

  We prioritise professional development, among other things by offering access to courses and other relevant activities. Socialising is also very important at GEUS, and we have a rich social life with a staff club, an art association and more.

  At GEUS, we prioritise the well-being of every single employee. We prioritise that the Heads of Departments are close to the employees, and we have flexible working hours that allow you to organise your life so that there is time for what matters to you. If you need to work from home occasionally, that is also possible.

  Furthermore, we have a gym with associated physiotherapists.

  Salary and conditions of employment
 The position as Professor is permanent. Salary and terms of employment are in accordance with the relevant trade union agreement. Supplements can be negotiated according to skills.

  The appointment area is the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Utilities and its institutions.

  The Ministry of Climate, Energy and Utilities considers diversity to be an asset and encourages anyone regardless of gender, age, religion or ethnicity to seek the position.

  Additional information
 If you would like additional information, please contact the Head of Department, Mikael Pedersen on telephone +45 22 21 65 75, e-mail mp@geus.dk, or Managing Director, Lars Nielsen, on telephone +45 91 33 38 70, e-mail larni@geus.dk.

  If you are an international applicant, you can read more about living and working in Denmark on GEUS’ website.

  Are you interested?
 Please write the application in English and include a letter of motivation, your PhD diploma and CV incl. your ORCID, as well as a complete list of publications with 1) a separate indication of peer-reviewed journal articles and 2) an indication of publications where you have been either the lead or senior author.

  Please include in the application the relevant academic works that you wish to be included in the professor assessment (max. 10). Please enclose other material that documents your research and teaching qualifications.

  You are requested to include a 2-3-page account that refers to your most important academic work with relevance to the position. Finally, you are encouraged to write a one-page explanation of your plans for the development of the field. In addition to the material that you would like to be included in the assessment, the assessment committee may choose to include further material in their assessment. It is your responsibility to send the material to the committee upon request.
 
 It is mandatory to include your updated ResearcherID and/or ORCID, which will be used to assess your publication record in Web of Science. Any recently accepted or submitted publications may be added separately to the list of publications.
 
 We must have your application at the latest on Monday 9 November 2026 (Danish time).

  Applications or other material received after the deadline will not be considered.

  The appointment procedure
 A professional assessment committee consisting of one internal and two to four external assessors at minimum professor level will carry out an individual assessment of all applicants’ professional qualifications, and the applicants will be assessed as qualified or unqualified for the position. Afterwards, an internal employment committee will decide which of the professionally qualified candidates will be invited for a job interview. This procedure is in accordance with the “Order on employment and assessment of scientific staff at the Geological Survey of Denmark and Greenland § 4 and 7”.

jobs.description:
How can coastal vegetation help protect our coastlines from waves and flooding? Understanding how waves interact with vegetation is key to exploring its potential for coastal protection and climate adaptation. Are you interested in combining fluid mechanics, mathematical analysis and numerical modelling to help answer this question.

Then join us for a 3-year PhD fellowship in coastal engineering at the Technical University of Denmark (DTU), Department of Civil and Mechanical Engineering, Section for Fluid Mechanics, Coastal and Maritime Engineering.

Your PhD research will play an integral part in the project “Marine advection and dissipation in the vegetated coastal environment”, financed by the Independent Research Fund Denmark.

You will collaborate with researchers at DTU and DHI in Denmark, as well as at University College Dublin, Ireland and Northeastern University, USA.

Responsibilities 
Your primary tasks will be to develop analytical and numerical models for waves interacting with coastal vegetation. Particular emphasis will be placed on the wave-averaged flow generated by surface waves and on the changes introduced by vegetation canopies.

The research will include:

• Development and validation of models for wave-induced mean velocity profiles over vegetated beds under regular waves.
• Extension of these models to irregular wave fields, including derivation of wave-averaged shear-stress distributions and mean velocity profiles.
• Investigation of undertow and circulation currents above vegetated beds in the surf zone under breaking waves.
• Development of a cross-shore momentum balance describing wave-induced changes in mean water level and the potential reduction of storm-surge flooding by coastal vegetation.
• Numerical simulations using computational fluid dynamics 
• Application of advanced turbulence models for surface-wave flows, modified to account for vegetation.
• Validation of the developed models against existing high-quality laboratory datasets.
• Development of practical parameterizations suitable for implementation in larger-scale coastal and hydrodynamic models.
The project combines fundamental fluid mechanics with applications directly relevant to coastal protection and climate adaptation. A major scientific objective is to move beyond conventional empirical vegetation models and instead explicitly account for the modification of the wave-induced velocity field within and above vegetation canopies.

Qualifications
We are looking for candidates with a strong background in one or more of the following areas:

• Coastal or ocean engineering
• Fluid mechanics or hydrodynamics
• Computational fluid dynamics
• Environmental hydraulics
• Applied mathematics or a closely related field
Experience with numerical modelling, programming and/or CFD is highly desirable. Experience with turbulence modelling, wave mechanics or coastal hydrodynamics would be advantageous, but is not essential. Strong mathematical skills and an interest in combining theoretical analysis with numerical modelling are important.

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures.

The period of employment is 3 years. Starting date is anticipated as 1 February 2027, or according to mutual agreement. The position is a full-time position. 

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information 
Further information may be obtained from Professor David R. Fuhrman (drfu@dtu.dk).

You can read more about Department of Civil and Mechanical Engineering at www.construct.dtu.dk.

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 10 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time). Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it. 

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.
